correspondence.component_scope: Selected southeastern opening and northern bends
correspondence.finding: No independent original map was acquired for the selected opening and its northward bends. The supplied selected path is orientation only and cannot establish a natural channel, lake passage or name.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected northward middle corridor and northwestward turn
correspondence.finding: No primary cartography establishes the entire middle succession, each intervening join or any selected lake or tributary connection. Nearby place names and regional membership are not substitutes for this missing correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected lower northwestward and westward corridor
correspondence.finding: The successfully read survey metadata places a company project in the McBean Bay and Brodeur River areas, but its textual extent and place labels do not show the selected route or its joins. The linked assessment publication was unavailable. Brodeur River remains an untested local-area lead, not a mapped component candidate.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected final western bends and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The actual last stored part and endpoint were retained in the source-assessment scope. No original cartography establishes their channel connection, receiving water or actual terminal setting. A nearby named river point was not substituted for this endpoint.

correspondence.component_scope: Western selected opening and eastward Jim Hogg County plain passage
correspondence.finding: The readable original covers the selected western opening, its initial eastward and northward bends, the long eastward continuation and every stored join across the Jim Hogg County plain. Roads, contours, isolated small water features and separately mapped intermittent channels are visible. No continuous mapped waterway follows the complete selected opening or its eastward through-passage. The northern channels and nearby water symbols cannot supply the missing selected connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward selected approach across the Jim Hogg–Brooks County surroundings toward Vargas Creek
correspondence.finding: The contiguous sources cover the selected southeastern continuation, southward turn and approach to the separately mapped Vargas Creek west of Tacubaya. This route traverses road, contour, vegetation and scattered small-water settings. The full selected through-waterway and its transfer into Vargas Creek are not established by the cartography. This is a concrete dryland-connection gap, not an exact-bank or individual-vertex requirement.

correspondence.component_scope: Mapped Vargas Creek middle corridor and its eastern small-lake setting
correspondence.finding: Repeated Vargas Creek labels identify the dashed blue channel running southeast across the FM755 surroundings and then east along the Brooks–Starr/Hidalgo county-boundary setting. The selected middle route corresponds to this corridor at ordinary regional scale, including the intermediate bends and the tributary-entry setting. Local generalized offsets and the selected northerly loop are not treated as exact bank failures. The source carries the mapped creek east to a small lake; it does not extend that named creek through the later selected cross-plain route. Perennial flow, formal name limits and a uniform whole-system name are not established.
correspondence.bounded_component_scope: Parts 12–14 and the western portion of part 15; the later eastward extension within part 15 is treated separately.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected transfer beyond the Vargas Creek small-lake setting and across US281
correspondence.finding: After the mapped Vargas Creek/lake setting, the selected route proceeds east across the plain and US281. Readable cartography shows road and ranch-land context and separately mapped drainage south/east of the highway, but does not establish the selected waterway across the intervening land. The creek name on the western side and an unrelated mapped stream on the eastern side are insufficient to establish this through-link.
correspondence.bounded_component_scope: Eastern portion of part 15, then parts 16–17.

correspondence.component_scope: Unnamed channel segment and selected bypass through the Callo Padrones small-water surroundings
correspondence.finding: The selected route briefly corresponds at ordinary corridor scale to an unnamed dashed blue channel approaching the mapped Callo Padrones waterbody. It then passes north of that waterbody and continues southeast through scattered small-water and contour settings. The source does not establish the selected bypass, the complete small-water transfers or their continuation. Callo Padrones and the separately labelled El Callo provide nearby geographic context only; neither is imposed as a river name or treated as proof that the selected route passes through a lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected southern turn and long northeastward inland passage
correspondence.finding: The originals cover the actual southernmost turn, the subsequent northerly and northeasterly sequence, every stored intermediate join, road crossings and the many isolated or clustered small waterbodies of the inland plain. They do not depict a continuous waterway or an explicit natural/managed through-connection along this complete selected passage. Common lowland setting, nearby blue polygons and the model line are not substituted for hydraulic or geographic through-link evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected eastward US77 crossing and southeastward approach to Cayo Soledad
correspondence.finding: The source spans the selected US77 crossing south of Armstrong, its eastward continuation, the southeastward bends and the complete approach to Cayo Soledad. It shows dryland/vegetation, ranch roads, contours and isolated waters, but no continuous channel along the selected through-passage to the western end of Cayo Soledad. The short final approach overlaps the lagoon setting; that local overlap does not close the preceding inland gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Bounded Cayo Soledad waterbody passage
correspondence.finding: The original directly labels Cayo Soledad on the elongated blue-outlined, stippled coastal waterbody. The selected eastward segment runs within its ordinary generalized corridor before turning northeast. This supports a bounded local waterbody name and passage, without assigning Cayo Soledad to the preceding inland route or asserting present inundation or exact shorelines.
correspondence.bounded_component_scope: Eastern end of part 34, all of short part 35 and the initial portion of part 36, before the selected northeastward coastal transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected northeast/east transfer from Cayo Soledad toward the coastal lagoon edge
correspondence.finding: After Cayo Soledad, the selected route turns northeast across the mapped shore and marsh/land setting, then east to the tidal lagoon edge. The source depicts the coastal marsh and a separate northern tidal inlet, but no complete channel along this selected transfer. The intervening wetland and coastal proximity do not establish the missing through-connection. This is not a claim that exchange is impossible or a diagnosis of a model error.
correspondence.bounded_component_scope: Middle portion of the final stored part, after leaving the Cayo Soledad corridor and before the actual endpoint.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual final endpoint at the western tidal-lagoon edge east of Kenedy County
correspondence.finding: The actual selected endpoint was inspected at the blue tidal-lagoon shoreline and indented coastal-marsh edge, north of the mapped Rincón de la Soledad setting. It was not replaced with Cayo Soledad, an upstream channel end or a nearby named feature. The generalized coastal terminal setting is established; an ordinary named-river mouth and the preceding unproved marsh through-connection are not. A name for the terminal lagoon is not assigned from these bounded views.
correspondence.bounded_component_scope: Actual endpoint of the final stored part.

correspondence.component_scope: headward_opening
correspondence.finding: The western selected opening lies in a small-lake and stream landscape leading north and then east into the larger irregular lake succession. The original shows these associated waters and their connecting channel setting. No feeder hydronym, definitive natural source or perennial-flow claim is established.

correspondence.component_scope: western_lake_succession
correspondence.finding: The selected eastward and then southeast/eastward succession corresponds to the mapped irregular lakes and connecting streams before the large central lake. The later northeast turn toward that central lake is distinguishable from separate southern lake and stream arrivals. Names and current flow conditions are unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: long_central_lake_passage
correspondence.finding: The original shows a large irregular lake with a broad western part and a long southeast-reaching arm, including islands and northern bays. The selection crosses this connected lake and follows its eastern end. The large VICTORIA lettering and thematic management boundaries are not hydronyms or river geometry.

correspondence.component_scope: central_lake_outlet_and_eastern_lakes
correspondence.finding: The selected northeast turn from the long central lake and its ensuing eastward course correspond to mapped stream links and the adjoining eastern lake. The map distinguishes northern incoming lake/stream branches from the eastward selected continuation. No name is established for these individual waters.

correspondence.component_scope: southeastern_descent_to_lower_river
correspondence.finding: From the eastern lake the selection turns southeast through smaller connected waters and channels to the more substantial eastward lower stream. The original depicts this connected descent and associated side branches at ordinary regional/corridor scale. No exact channel-bank or modeled-vertex correspondence is claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: lower_eastward_channel_and_widenings
correspondence.finding: The original shows the distinctive eastward lower river, elongated widenings, the larger lake-like widening and successive northern and southern stream arrivals. These align with the selected lower corridor to the eastern map edge. The part of the last listed subline beyond that edge is not established by this map.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern_sheet_crossing_and_lower_northward_reach
correspondence.finding: The selected path turns north after leaving the eastern Washburn Lake map coverage. No successful adjacent-map acquisition was confirmed, and no adjacent original pixels were read. Its lake connections, material lower joins and northward continuity therefore remain source-material pending.

correspondence.component_scope: final_lake_channel_connections_and_actual_terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected final northward/northeast approach and actual terminal are outside the read original. No receiving bay, river mouth, terminal-channel connection or whole-system river identity is established from source evidence. Nearby coastal labels elsewhere on the Washburn Lake map are not substituted for the actual terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: Western unnamed opening and first named-course junction
correspondence.finding: The complete western opening is exposed in the bounded MMA hydrography. The selected west-to-east approach follows the ordinary corridor of an unnamed Quebrada feature into the Río Chaike o Chico network. Its extreme first modeled position extends a short distance west of the mapped line end, without a separate large unviewed corridor. The unnamed feeder remains unnamed; the downstream name is not retroactively assigned to it. The historical IGN view has no cartography over this western opening and is not used for it.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper eastward named course and northward bend
correspondence.finding: MMA features directly named Río Chaike o Chico expose the eastward upper reach, tributary joins and turn toward the north. IGN labels the same general Chilean river corridor R. Ciaike. Both depict the ordinary valley/channel sequence; the minor angular departures of the selected rendering are not treated as exact-bank evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward river sequence and intermediate junctions
correspondence.finding: Both originals cover the northward passage and every intervening selected part. MMA attaches Río de los Pozuelos to a source segment along part of this connecting network, leaves the following short Río segment unnamed, and uses Río Chaike o Chico again on a later source segment. IGN depicts the same connected regional course in the Ciaike setting. The different source segment labels are preserved rather than forcing one scalar label across each component.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward departure from the natural course toward the border connector
correspondence.finding: The originals expose this entire transition. The selected line turns north away from the mapped river toward the international-border setting. The actual mapped watercourse continues east farther south, downstream of the Laguna Timone outlet junction toward Estancia Brazo Norte. Readable land/border cartography alone does not positively identify the selected departure as a particular non-river feature or establish a through-waterway; this transition remains part of the concrete material-pending gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Both parts of the border-aligned middle fragment and its joins
correspondence.finding: Both parts and both adjoining transitions were inspected in the existing originals. IGN places the nearly east-west selection in the border-marker/land setting north of the river, while MMA exposes the watercourse farther south. The source river passes east from the Laguna Timone junction through the Estancia Brazo Norte setting and then bends northeast toward Pali Aike. The sources do not establish a natural channel, lake passage or managed transfer along the selected northern connector, nor positively identify its whole extent as a specific non-river feature. This selected through-connection is therefore unresolved and material-pending. Laguna Timone is off-route tributary-lake context.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward return from the border connector and re-entry into the river corridor
correspondence.finding: The originals expose the short return south from the border-aligned fragment and northeastward re-entry near Pali Aike. The initial selected return lacks an established waterway or positively identified non-river explanation linking it back from the border connector. Farther east, the selected passage rejoins the mapped Ciaike/Chico river corridor. The gap is limited to the connector and its adjoining departure/return, rather than the entire lower fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Argentine Río Chico valley and intermediate bends
correspondence.finding: The historical IGN original covers the northeastward valley, its southern tributary joins and the bends past the Pali Aike/Andeón, Tres Hermanos and Bella Vista settings. Its river label is R. Chico. Nearby Laguna Pali Aike and Laguna Bismarck lie away from the selected river passage and are not converted into through-lake connectors. All stored parts and their joins are visible at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Río Chico, final stored parts and actual estuarine endpoint
correspondence.finding: The IGN original covers the entire lower northeastward Río Chico valley past Bella Vista and La Vega, the final eastward approach near Río Chico/Chimen Aike, and the actual selected endpoint at the mapped estuarine foreshore beside Río Gallegos. The river opens into the same coastal receiving-water setting as the Gallegos mouth; this is the actual selected terminal rather than an upstream confluence or merely a nearby name. Historical shoreline symbols do not establish present tidal stage, precise banks or current inundation.
